::: {#rem-backprop-memory}

#### What backpropagation stores

The backward steps of @sol-manual-backward reuse `z1` and `h` from the forward pass,
so PyTorch keeps every intermediate result that a later backward step needs
until `.backward()` has run.
That memory grows with the number of layers and with the batch size,
and it is often what limits the batch size on a GPU.
Code run inside `torch.no_grad()`,
such as computing test [accuracy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/metrics.html#def-accuracy),
records nothing and keeps nothing.

:::
